topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, reviews prior context, and outlines the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and oncogenic signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous proliferation and survival signaling.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how differentiation blocks prevent progenitor and epithelial cells from maturing and exiting the cell cycle.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cancer cells evade programmed cell death by altering the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress-induced genome protection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells bypass senescence via telomerase activation and how cellular stress signals converge on p53 to restrict cell division.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways such as glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations produce oncometabolites that drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses the requirement for new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients to expanding tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomic features of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multi-step metastatic cascade, its biological inefficiencies, liquid biopsy monitoring, and associated genomic alterations.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing thoughts and housekeeping remarks.
